claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: For ℓ≥k, adjoining ℓ−k isolated K2 components with their endpoints as new terminal pairs is polynomial and forces exactly those added edge-paths. Restriction and extension therefore preserve the answer. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, it cannot span components or occur inside K2, so the promise is preserved. For k=1, connectivity is necessary and sufficient: a shortest terminal path is induced, since any chord shortens it, and BFS/DFS is linear. For fixed k, lists of simple path vertices form polynomial-size certificates, and path validity, disjointness, chords, and cross-path edges are polynomially checkable. The exact small-instance checker also passed 1,098 one-pair graphs and 64 two-pair graphs.
claims.search_method: Direct reduction and certificate proof, supplemented by exhaustive exact small-instance enumeration.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: If u-x-y-v is a shortest three-edge path and deg(u),deg(v)≥3, choose two neighbors of u other than x and two of v other than y. Shortestness excludes the connector vertices and forces the two neighbor pairs to be disjoint; otherwise u and v would be at distance at most two. These eight distinct vertices and the seven required edges form H3 as a subgraph. For degeneracy, every graph of minimum degree at least seven contains every eight-vertex tree: embed a rooted tree parent-first; when embedding its jth vertex, at most j−2≤6 neighbors of the parent image are already used, while that image has at least seven neighbors. Thus no subgraph of an H3-free graph has minimum degree seven. A 6-degeneracy ordering gives at most 6(n−7)+21=6n−21 edges for n≥7. K7 proves sharpness. Finally, a geodesic of length at least three in a connected minimum-degree-three graph has first and fourth vertices at distance exactly three, contradicting the distance lemma.
claims.witness: K7 has only seven vertices, so it is H3-free, while its degeneracy is six and it has 21=6·7−21 edges.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal and metric graph proof from the eight-vertex structure of H3.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: Every subdivision vertex has degree two, so an H3 center would have to be original. A three-edge simple path starting from an original vertex either starts down an R-corridor and remains at a subdivision vertex after three edges, or starts with an M-edge, reaches another original after one edge, and—because M is a matching—must then enter an R-corridor and again finish at a subdivision vertex. Thus no possible centers are joined by a three-edge path. With original terminals, degree-two corridor interiors force any entered R-corridor to be traversed completely. Contracting these traversals gives vertex-disjoint simple paths in R∪M, and lifting reverses this. Subdivided unused R-edges create no adjacency among selected originals; the only possible extra selected-selected edges are unsubdivided M-edges, so the stated matching condition is exactly the inducedness condition. Taking M empty and R=K_m yields an H3-free graph with a K_m minor, hence treewidth at least m−1. Exhaustive checking passed all 328 constructions G(R,M) for |V(R)|≤4 and 2,799 one- or two-pair family comparisons.
claims.witness: For every m, take M=∅ and R=K_m; contracting the four-edge corridors produces a K_m minor.
claims.search_method: Center-path case analysis and exact corridor contraction/lifting proof, supplemented by exhaustive small-construction enumeration.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: Let B contain the b vertices of degree at least three. Every component of G−B is a path, isolated vertex, or cycle and has at most two B-attachments. A terminal-free component is usable only as a corridor between two distinct B vertices; one two-edge representative per unordered pair suffices, for at most binom(b,2) new vertices. In a terminal-bearing component, mark its terminals and attachment occurrences and delete unmarked tails. Every gap between consecutive marks is either avoided or traversed completely because its internal vertices are nonterminals of degree two. A length-one gap must remain an edge, while every longer gap can be replaced by a two-edge path; expansion and contraction preserve precisely the relevant adjacencies. Detached one-terminal cycles are NO, and cycles with at least two terminals are treated cyclically. Besides B, there are at most 2k retained terminals. A path component with t≥1 outside-B terminals has at most t+1≤2t gaps, and a cycle has t, so at most 4k gap representatives are needed overall. The total is therefore b+binom(b,2)+2k+4k. Exhaustive search on this bounded graph is a function only of k+b. As a counterexample search, the exact checker found no mismatch on all 33,856 labelled graphs of orders four through six with two disjoint pairs.
claims.search_method: Complete maximum-degree-two component and marked-gap case analysis, plus exhaustive exact small-instance comparison.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: The host has seven vertices and therefore cannot contain the eight-vertex H3. Exact enumeration finds precisely two simple s1-t1 paths; s1-x-t1 is the unique shortest, of length two. The only simple s2-t2 path is s2-t2, and edge xs2 conflicts with the shortest path. Conversely, s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2 are induced, vertex-disjoint, and have no edge between them. Thus a solution exists but none can contain the globally shortest first path.
claims.witness: Vertices {s1,t1,x,s2,t2,y,z}; edges {s1x,xt1,xs2,s2t2,s1y,yz,zt1}; failed shortest path s1-x-t1; surviving linkage (s1-y-z-t1, s2-t2).
claims.search_method: Exact enumeration of all simple paths, induced-linkage tests, and H3 subgraph testing.

target_evidence: The exact target requests a complexity classification for every fixed k. The draft classifies only k=1. NP membership and monotone padding do not decide polynomial-time solvability versus hardness for k≥2; FPT in k+b does not specialize to a fixed-k polynomial algorithm on all H3-free graphs because b is unbounded; and the degeneracy, routing, treewidth, and greedy-obstruction results likewise do not classify any fixed k≥2. These are correct, relevant partial advances, and the final writeup explicitly states that the all-k classification remains unresolved. Therefore the target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, and claimed_resolution="PARTIAL" is ACCURATE.
